invoice-approval.reveal_note: Everything reads professionally and the domain looks right at a glance. The tell is subtle: the fake domain has an added hyphen (rossum-supply.com vs rossumsupply.com), and the bank details changed without the phone confirmation finance policy requires.
red_flags: Sender domain rossum-supply.com has an extra hyphen
Bank details changed with no phone confirmation
Sent late in the day to catch finance in a rush
invoice-approval.what_you_can_do: Phone the supplier on a number you already hold before changing any bank details.

executive-travel-request.reveal_note: The display name and writing style closely match the CFO, but the actual sender address is a personal Outlook account rather than the company one, and the request routes payment through personal Venmo instead of the corporate travel system finance normally uses.
red_flags: Sent from a personal Outlook address, not the company's
Asks you to pay by Venmo and skip the travel system
Urgent and 'no time' for the normal process
executive-travel-request.what_you_can_do: Call Marcus on his known number. Flights are booked through Concur, never with personal payment apps.

eventbrite-ticket.subject_label: An event ticket with a QR code
eventbrite-ticket.reveal_note: The real ticket has an entry QR code and a link to eventbrite.com. The fake, from eventbrite-entry-pass.top, says your ticket is invalid and has no link, only a QR code that hides where it leads.
red_flags: Sender domain eventbrite-entry-pass.top is not eventbrite.com
No link, only a QR code: you can't see the destination
The QR leads to a sign-in page for your password
eventbrite-ticket.what_you_can_do: Don't scan a QR code from an email that asks you to sign in. Open the Eventbrite app or site yourself.

compliance-training.reveal_note: The fake borrows the CEO's title to scare you, but comes from meridianfreight-hr.com, not meridianfreight.com, orders you not to discuss it, and links to a login page over http.
red_flags: Sender domain meridianfreight-hr.com is not meridianfreight.com
Uses the CEO's authority and a threat of discipline
'Do not discuss this with colleagues' stops you checking
'Sent from my iPhone' is a cheap trust trick
Link opens a login page over plain http
compliance-training.what_you_can_do: Check with the sender or IT on a channel you already trust. A genuine directive never needs you to hide it.

ariba-approval.reveal_note: Both look the same. The real one comes from ariba.com and tells you to open Ariba from your own bookmark. The fake comes from ariba-approvals.com and gives you a link to a look-alike login.
ariba-approval.what_you_can_do: Approve invoices only inside Ariba, opened from your own bookmark.

ceo-desk.subject_label: A message from the CEO, on your phone
ceo-desk.reveal_note: The display name is identical, so on a phone you only see Daniel Koh. The fake address ends in .co, not .com, and the message builds trust before asking for something.
ceo-desk.what_you_can_do: If an executive asks for an unspecified favour, call or message them on a channel you already use.

hr-statement.reveal_note: The real email points you to Workday. The fake comes from meridianfrieght.com (ie and ei swapped) and wants your bank details before you can see anything.
hr-statement.what_you_can_do: Open Workday yourself. HR never needs bank details to show you a statement.

teams-guest.subject_label: A Teams meeting invite, on your phone
teams-guest.reveal_note: Both show Microsoft Teams. The real address is email.teams.microsoft.com; the fake swaps the dots for hyphens, so the real domain is email-teams-microsoft.com.
teams-guest.what_you_can_do: Join meetings from your calendar or the Teams app, never through a link that asks you to sign in.

aws-mfa.reveal_note: The real notice comes from amazon.com and tells you to use your own bookmark. The fake comes from amazon-aws-security.com and gives you a link to a look-alike IAM page.
aws-mfa.what_you_can_do: Review IAM activity from your own bookmark and report the email to Security.

zoom-invoice.subject_label: A Zoom invoice, on your phone
zoom-invoice.reveal_note: On a phone both say Zoom. The fake address is billing@zoom.us.invoice-center.net, where zoom.us is only a prefix: the real domain is invoice-center.net.
zoom-invoice.what_you_can_do: Read a domain from right to left, just before the first slash. Download invoices from zoom.us after signing in yourself.

calendar-invite.reveal_note: Nearly identical. The fake comes from googIe.com, with a capital I instead of the l in google, which is hard to see in most fonts, and it adds a sign-in step.
red_flags: A capital I, not an l
calendar-invite.what_you_can_do: Accept invites from your calendar app. If a sign-in appears, stop and check the address letter by letter.

recruiter-pdf.subject_label: A recruiter message, on your phone
recruiter-pdf.reveal_note: A job message is a favourite lure. The fake comes from maersk-careers.com, flatters you, asks for secrecy and attaches a file that ends .pdf.html: a web page pretending to be a PDF.
recruiter-pdf.what_you_can_do: Look up the role on the company's real careers page. Never open a file ending .pdf.html.

servicenow-ticket.reveal_note: The ticket number and wording are right, because the attacker knew about your VPN problem. The fake ends in .co, not .com, and asks for your network password to 'confirm'.
servicenow-ticket.what_you_can_do: IT never needs your password to close a ticket. Reply to the ticket or call the Service Desk.

maersk-bol.reveal_note: In a freight company this is a daily email. The real one sends you to the Maersk portal; the fake comes from maersk-docs.com with an .html attachment that opens a fake login.
red_flags: Opens a file, not the portal
maersk-bol.what_you_can_do: Check booking documents in the carrier's portal, opened from your bookmark.

oauth-consent.subject_label: A Microsoft account notice, on your phone
oauth-consent.reveal_note: Everything matches except one letter: the fake comes from microsft.com, missing an o. Real Microsoft emails tell you to review apps at account.microsoft.com yourself.
oauth-consent.what_you_can_do: Review connected apps by going to account.microsoft.com yourself.

xero-paynow.reveal_note: The real invoice comes from post.xero.com with a link to an invoice page. The fake comes from post-xero.com and asks you to pay with a PayNow QR code, which hides who actually gets the money.
red_flags: Asks you to pay by QR
A QR hides who gets paid
xero-paynow.what_you_can_do: Pay invoices only from a PO or supplier record you can verify, never from a QR code in an email.

singpass-device.subject_label: A Singpass alert, on your phone
singpass-device.reveal_note: Real: singpass.gov.sg. Fake: singpass-gov.sg, where a hyphen replaces the dot. The real alert tells you to use the Singpass app instead of a link.
red_flags: Asks you to verify by link
singpass-device.what_you_can_do: Report suspicious logins in the Singpass app. Never verify your identity through an email link.

workday-expense.reveal_note: Same words, same layout. The fake comes from workdayy.com (a double y) and links to a copy of the Workday sign-in page.
workday-expense.what_you_can_do: Approve things from the Workday app or your own bookmark, not from the email.

wise-transfer.subject_label: A payment update, on your phone
wise-transfer.reveal_note: The real update comes from wise.com and tells you to track it in the app. The fake's domain is transfer-status.net (wise.com is only a prefix) and it asks for 'new bank details', a classic payment fraud.
wise-transfer.what_you_can_do: Confirm any change of bank details by phone, using a number you already hold.

cpf-statement.reveal_note: The real email says CPF never asks for your Singpass password by email. The fake comes from cpf-board.com, not a .gov.sg address, and asks for exactly that.
cpf-statement.what_you_can_do: Government sites end in .gov.sg. Go to cpf.gov.sg yourself and log in with Singpass.

sms-ceo-newnumber.reveal_note: The real message shows Daniel Koh because he is in your contacts. The fake arrives from an unknown number, claims it is Daniel's new one, and asks for a vague favour first.
red_flags: A vague ask to hook you
sms-ceo-newnumber.what_you_can_do: Call Daniel on the number you already have before you reply to a 'new number' message.

sms-singpass-code.reveal_note: Both show SINGPASS. The real text only holds a code and says to ignore it if you didn't ask. The fake raises an alarm and links to singpass-verify.sg.
sms-singpass-code.what_you_can_do: Real Singpass texts carry a code, not a link. Use the Singpass app to check your activity.

sms-google-code.reveal_note: A real verification text is just the code. The fake adds a line and a link, google-help.co, to cancel it.
red_flags: Adds a link to a code text
sms-google-code.what_you_can_do: If you didn't ask for a code, change your password in the Google app or at google.com, not through the text.

qr-guest-wifi.reveal_note: The printed address is the same, which is what makes this hard. The fake is a sticker over the real code, and it asks guests for a work login. The QR really opens meridianfreight-guest.com.
red_flags: A sticker over the real code
Guests don't have a work login
qr-guest-wifi.what_you_can_do: Guest Wi-Fi never needs a work login. Ask reception for the password instead of scanning an unexpected code.

qr-paynow-counter.subject_label: A PayNow code at a cafe counter
qr-paynow-counter.reveal_note: Everything matches except two details: the fake is a sticker over the original, and its UEN differs from the one on the shop's receipts. Scanning pays a private account, not Kopi Corner.
red_flags: A sticker over the real code
Same words as the real one
qr-paynow-counter.what_you_can_do: Check the payee name in your banking app before you confirm. If it isn't the shop's name, don't pay.

qr-summit-badge.reveal_note: The sign looks the same, with no sticker. The printed address is missing an m (sgcybersumit.sg), and the fake asks you to sign in with LinkedIn for an agenda.
red_flags: QR can't show where it leads
qr-summit-badge.what_you_can_do: An agenda never needs a login. Read the printed address letter by letter before you scan.

it-vpn-certificate.subject_label: An IT email about your VPN certificate
it-vpn-certificate.reveal_note: The real email says the certificate renews by itself and no action is needed. The fake comes from meridianfreight-vpn.com, claims it has expired and links to a page to reinstall it.
it-vpn-certificate.what_you_can_do: IT never sends installers by email link. Raise a ticket on the Service Desk portal from your own bookmark.

singtel-town-hall.reveal_note: The real email is from singtel.com and points you to the staff intranet. The fake comes from singtei.com, with an i in place of the l, and asks you to register with your staff login.
red_flags: An i where the l should be
singtel-town-hall.what_you_can_do: Use the staff intranet from your own bookmark. Read an address letter by letter before you sign in.

singtel-cyber-training.subject_label: A Singtel training reminder, on your phone
singtel-cyber-training.reveal_note: Both look the same on a phone. The real email tells you to use your own bookmark. The fake comes from singtel-learning.com and gives you a link that asks for your staff login.
singtel-cyber-training.what_you_can_do: Tap the sender name to check the address, then open the learning portal from your own bookmark.

singtel-ceo-office.subject_label: An email from the Group CEO Office
singtel-ceo-office.reveal_note: The real email only says thank you and needs no action. The fake comes from singtel-group.com and asks for your mobile number, the first step of a phone scam.
singtel-ceo-office.what_you_can_do: Executives' offices don't ask for your number by email. Check with your manager before you reply.

singtel-benefits.subject_label: A Singtel benefits email, on your phone
singtel-benefits.reveal_note: The sender name matches on a phone. The real email says to use the HR portal from your bookmark. The fake comes from singte1.com, with a 1 in place of the l, and gives you a link.
red_flags: A 1 where the l should be
singtel-benefits.what_you_can_do: Tap the sender name to read the address letter by letter. Open the HR portal from your own bookmark.
